why: A count is not a comparison. These are the SORTED FAILURE IDENTITIES of each full-suite run, so a later reader can diff them instead of trusting a number, and so the matched pair survives the container that produced it.
how_each_run_was_made: a frozen `git archive <sha> | tar -x` checkout, its own freshly migrated database whose name is LOWER CASE (Postgres folds an unquoted CREATE DATABASE, while a DSN does not -- see GATE_HARNESS_DEFECT_MIXED_CASE_DB.json), `python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:randomly`. From the 21:37 pair onward, also `--timeout=180 --timeout-method=signal`, so a stall becomes one NAMED failure instead of a run with no summary. The pair is run CONCURRENTLY so both sides see the same machine load.

baseline_6d75275_rerun_2137.why_it_matters: Two hours later, on a different database, under concurrency, with the --timeout plugin added, the baseline's 178 failure IDENTITIES are byte-identical. That is what makes an identity diff on this suite a signal -- and a COUNT still is not one.
